description: Residents/landowners first noted expanding steaming ground and water reappearing along natural fractures at the Lower Sinter Terrace -- the first sign of renewed hydrothermal activity after decades of relative quiescence.

Steaming ground expanded measurably across the lower sinter terrace; previously dry/weakly-warm areas developed persistent vapor flux and moist, thermally altered soils. No focused vents or flowing water yet -- activity was primarily diffuse.

Character of activity shifted from diffuse degassing to localized venting: small seeps and weak springs appeared along fracture-controlled zones and at the base of the sinter mound. First evidence of shallow boiling and focused upward flow (intermittent splashing/'spitting').

Existing vents intensified: splashing increased, small pools formed and drained repeatedly, localized discharge points migrated along nearby fractures. Change now observable over days to weeks rather than months.

An uncapped, shallow (~15-20 m), abandoned well on the Lower Sinter Terrace unexpectedly erupted, shooting boiling water nearly 30 m high -- the first geyser-like activity documented at Steamboat in decades (abstract date; body text describes the eruption as occurring 'mid-June 2025').

The erupting pipe was capped shortly after the eruption. Discharge did not cease but instead shifted laterally, with new small springs and persistent spitting vents forming along adjacent fractures and sinter surfaces.
NBMG initiated an integrated monitoring program (water sampling/geochemistry, thermal drone surveys, continuous temperature logging, surface-feature mapping) in direct response to the eruption.

First nighttime calibrated thermal drone survey of the Lower Sinter Terrace area (~0.27 sq. area of interest); temperature loggers also deployed in the uncapped well, an actively steaming fissure, and the Steamboat Resort holding tank around this time (1-8 July 2025).

Second nighttime calibrated thermal drone survey, repeating the July flight paths/control points/processing methods to quantify change over time. Ground and vent temperatures measured cooler in October than July.
